sentences.text: Jeholosaurus was a small, bipedal dinosaur belonging to the neornithischian group that lived during the Early Cretaceous period.
The holotype specimen measures 71.1 centimeters in total length, with a tail that extends 35.6 centimeters.
Its skull is 6.3 centimeters long, while each lower jaw measures 5.9 centimeters.
The front of the upper jaw holds six teeth, whereas the back section contains at least thirteen.
The deep lower edge of the upper jaw suggests that fleshy cheeks may have been present to help manipulate food.
A unique trait is that the claw on the third toe is longer than the other bones of that same digit.
First found in 2000 near Beipiao City in Liaoning Province, the genus name translates to 'lizard from Jehol,' a historical region in western Liaoning and northern Hebei.
The primary specimen used to describe the genus is cataloged under the number IVPP V 12529.
By 2009, four additional specimens, including partial and complete skulls, were added to the known material.
Both known skulls are incomplete and required partial restoration to be studied fully.
Scientists propose that this animal might have been an omnivore because its front teeth look like those of meat-eaters while its back teeth are fan-shaped like those of plant-eaters.
It replaced its upper jaw teeth every 46 days, a rate faster than most basal ornithischians.
The foot possesses four metatarsals, with the third one measuring 5.5 centimeters and positioned more toward the front than the others.
The original researchers did not assign it to a specific family, classifying it only as Ornithischia incertae sedis.
Later studies placed the dinosaur in a basal position within the Ornithopoda.
A group containing Jeholosaurus, Haya, and Changchunsaurus was named Jeholosauridae, and the species is now classified within this family.
However, the Paleobi Database lists the family of Jeholosaurus as Thescelosauridae.
The fossils date to the Barremian stage of the Early Cretaceous, approximately 126 to 124 million years ago.
This animal lived during the early Cretaceous, roughly 124 million years ago, between the late Barremian and early Aptian in what is now Asia.
The holotype was found in the lower Yixian Formation dating to the early Aptian, approximately 126 million years ago.
The sedimentary layers consist of interbedded fluvial sandstone and tuff, believed to be deposited by a massive volcanic eruption covering an 80 to 96-kilometer radius.
The time range for Jeholosaurus is from the Barremian to the Aptian, between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago.
